newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Hibernian operating profit rises slightly.
newsitem.headline: Hibernian operating profit rises slightly.

text.p: Irish insurer Hibernian Group Plc said 1996 operating profit before tax was up slightly to 27.0 million Irish pounds against 26.8 million in calendar 1995.
The company said it was recommending a final dividend of 7.0 pence per share, a 15 percent increase over the final dividend in 1995.
The final dividend, together with the interim dividend of 3.1 pence already paid, makes a total dividend of 10.0 pence per share for the full year, a 13.5 percent increase over 1995, it said.

The company said its life and pensions operations increased operating profits by 73 percent to 10.6 million pounds, driven primarily by significant growth in recurring premium income and cost efficiences.
This compensated for a 20 percent fall in operating profits from general insurance activities, the company said.

Operating profit from general insurance activities amounted to 16.4 million pounds against 20.6 million in 1995 with reduced profits in Ireland offsetting improvements in international reinsurance and UK operations.
Hibernian said it was competing in an increasingly crowded market place and would rely on innovation and quality for success.

The company said that the strength of the Irish economy would create opportunities for revenue development as the insurance cycle improves but the trading environment in core markets reamined very competitive.
It said it expects low interest rates to be sustained in the medium term, restricting the scope for investment income growth.
